title: security: rbac v2 enforce kms region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Marisol Chen
description:
Enforce KMS region pinning at RBAC v2 evaluation time and harden audit logging for KMS-related events. Motivation: customers have asked for stronger data residency guarantees when a KMS key is configured on a resource; previously RT policies were applied but audit logs did not always include sufficient metadata to prove region residency. This PR does three things: 1) Enforce region pinning at policy-evaluation time (configurable via feature flag) so that requests using a KMS key from a different region are denied when policy requires residency. 2) Augment audit log entries for requests that touch customer-managed KMS keys to include kms_key_id, kms_region, resolved_key_alias, and policy_evaluation_reason so compliance teams can reconstruct decisions. 3) Add a migration and rollout plan with a conservative opt-in rollout via feature flag and metrics to detect unintended denials. Checklist: - [x] Implement enforcement in RBAC policy evaluator with non-breaking default (feature flag off) - [x] Add audit log enrichment and schema bump (audit.kms_region v2) - [x] Add unit tests for policy evaluator and audit enrichment - [x] Add integration tests covering cross-region KMS usage and deny/allow cases - [x] Add metrics (rbac.kms_region_pin_denials, rbac.kms_region_pin_allowed_after_migration) - [x] Document upgrade/migration steps and operator-visible flags - [x] Add helm/installer flag to expose feature flag to Private customers - [x] Run security scan and perf microbenchmarks to validate overhead

Implementation notes: enforcement is implemented as an additional evaluation phase in redwood/services/rbac/policy_evaluator.py; the evaluator now resolves the effective kms_key metadata (region, key id, alias) via the KMS integration layer (redwood/integration/kms/client.go and client_py shim) before final allow/deny. When the feature flag rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce is enabled, any mismatch between resource residency required by policy and kms_key.region causes a DENY with a clear audit code (KMS_REGION_PIN_VIOLATION). To avoid availability regressions during rollout, the policy path falls back to a soft-audit mode when the feature flag is off and sets an audit marker but does not block the request. The audit schema change is additive and backward compatible: new fields are optional and included when present. Migration: operators should run the provided datafix job to ensure resources are annotated with kms_key metadata (scripts/migrations/annotate_kms_metadata.py) before flipping the enforce flag. Rollout plan in docs: enable on subset of tenants, monitor metrics for unexpected denials for 48 hours, then widen. Backport: small patch prepared for v2025.10.x (see backport branch).

review_comments: Ethan Walker: Nice work — can we avoid an extra KMS lookup for requests that already include resolved key metadata? Suggest caching resolved_key_alias in the resource cache.
Marisol Chen: Good call — added short-lived cache in the policy evaluator and unit tests to validate cache eviction.
Sara Liu: Audit enrichment looks good. Please ensure PII isn't leaked. Confirmed fields are key ids and aliases only; no plaintext key material.
Marisol Chen: Confirmed, security scan verifies no secret exposure; kms_key material is never logged.
Diego Morales: Integration test failed on first run due to async KMS client race; added deterministic wait and retried. Tests pass in CI now.
Ethan Walker: Approved after small nits were addressed.
release_notes: Enforce KMS region pinning at RBAC v2 evaluation time (opt-in via feature flag) and add richer audit logs for KMS usage. Operators must run annotate_kms_metadata migration before enabling enforcement. See docs/security/rbac_v2_kms_residency.md for rollout guidance.
